results.name: OYL-002 American Wheat
results.pofReason: Omega page (omegayeast.com/yeast/ales/american-wheat) re-fetched: 'Phenolic: No', 'fairly clean and lightly dry'. Multiple retailers confirm OYL-002 'Compares to WY1010' (Wyeast 1010 American Wheat) — a clean, non-phenolic American wheat strain. POF-negative is CORRECT for this strain. SIBLING/GROUP NOTE: the strainGroup 'wlp320' pairs OYL-002 with White Labs WLP320 American Hefeweizen, but this is a MIS-GROUPING — OYL-002 = WY1010 American Wheat lineage (clean), whereas the true WLP320 cross-lab equivalent is OYL-021 Hefeweizen Ale I, not OYL-002. They are genuinely different strains with different POF genotypes, so the group POF values legitimately differ (OYL-002 POF-, WLP320 POF+).
results.sta1Reason: Omega page: 'Diastatic: No'. WY1010-equivalent American wheat strain, attenuation 74-78% normal, non-diastatic. Consistent with WLP320 (also STA1-negative), so the STA1 group value is consistent even though the grouping itself is questionable on POF grounds.

results.name: WLP320 American Hefeweizen Ale Yeast
results.pofReason: White Labs official page (whitelabs.com, id=149) re-fetched: 'produces very slight banana and clove notes'. Clove = 4-vinyl-guaiacol, so the strain DOES carry functional PAD1+/FDC1+ and converts ferulic acid to 4-VG — POF+ by genotype, just milder than WLP300/Weihenstephan weizen yeast. The brief's rule applies: genotype-honest call is POF+ even though sensory intensity is low. SIBLING/GROUP NOTE: strainGroup 'wlp320' incorrectly pairs WLP320 (American Hefeweizen, POF+) with OYL-002 (American Wheat = WY1010 clean, POF-); these are different isolates (true WLP320 Omega analog is OYL-021), so POF correctly differs across the mis-grouped pair.
results.sta1Reason: White Labs page STA1 QC field: 'STA1: Negative'. Trust the lab's genetic QC. Attenuation 70-75% normal. Consistent with OYL-002 (STA1-negative).

results.name: 3638 Bavarian Wheat
results.pofReason: Wyeast product page (wyeastlab.com/product/bavarian-wheat) re-fetched: banana esters 'complemented nicely by clove and subtle vanilla phenolics.' Classic Bavarian weizen strain producing 4-VG clove — POF+ genotype. Matches WLP351-group siblings (OYL-025 'Phenolic: Yes').
results.sta1Reason: Recorded 'negative' is WRONG. 3638 is the same isolate as WLP351 / OYL-025 (suregork/Langdon 2019 genome decoding: 'WLP351 identified as a S. cerevisiae x S. uvarum hybrid that possesses STA1'; MTF/Langdon: 3638 = WLP351). STA1 is genetic, so 3638 must match its tested-positive siblings. The WLP351 lineage carries the 1162-bp STA1 promoter deletion (Langdon/Krogerus 2019, PMC6719335), i.e. it is weakly diastatic and attenuates normally (~70-76%) — so the normal attenuation is NOT evidence of STA1-negative. Flip negative -> positive; this is the adjudicated value.

results.name: OYL-025 Bavarian Wheat I
results.pofReason: Omega page (omegayeast.com/yeast/ales/bavarian-wheat) re-fetched: 'Phenolic: Yes'; predominant clove and pepper. Bavarian weizen = canonical 4-VG clove producer, POF+ genotype. Consistent with WLP351-group siblings (3638, WLP351).
results.sta1Reason: Omega page: 'This strain tests positive for the STA1 gene, an indicator of S. cerevisiae var. diastaticus'; 'Diastatic: Yes'. The 'sta1+ but low attenuation' flag is NOT a contradiction: the WLP351/OYL-025 weizen lineage carries the 1162-bp STA1 promoter-deletion variant (~100x lower expression, Langdon/Krogerus 2019), so it is genuinely STA1+ yet attenuates a normal 72-78%. Trust the lab's genetic positive over the attenuation-based doubt.
